$comment: See host.schema.json's own $comment for why every field lives inside the `environment:` object, name included. No container_fallback_policy -- explicitly dropped ('No policy knob in the environment file'). access is documented in the Operating a live build section, not the main Environment example, but is a real field. teams is required only when there is no `extends`.

environment.description: An environment: one game or test -- the file a build starts from. Lives at the repo root, one per event, and never mentions a builder or an IP supply so it can be reused year to year on any hoster.

schema.description: Schema/format version of this environment file.

teams.description: Number of teams. Every team gets an identical copy of the topology below -- nothing is ever templated per team.

root_password.description: A password stored in the clear on purpose -- content credentials exist to be found during the competition, not to be real secrets.

dns.description: DNS settings for the environment. A records for every host/container are generated automatically; this adds anything else.
dns.example:
dns:
  type: bind
  root_domain: allports.local
  dns_servers: [8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4]
  ntp_servers: [129.6.15.28]
  records:
    - { name: intranet, type: CNAME, target: web01 }
    - { name: mail, type: MX, target: mail01, priority: 10 }

access.description: The planned student access schedule (e.g. closing overnight on a multi-day event). Per-team overrides during a live event happen from the UI/API, not here.

vars.description: Key/value data cascaded down to every network, host, and container in this environment.

tags.description: Labels for searching, grouping, and ad-hoc targeting.

findings.description: Findings that belong to the environment as a whole.
findings.example:
findings:
  - severity: 3
    difficulty: 1
    description: Root password is stored in the clear (intentional)

networks.description: The topology: for each network, which hosts/containers are placed on it, how many copies, and their addresses. The only place hosts, containers, and networks are connected to each other. (Which of a host's ports are externally reachable is `public:` on the host itself, not here.)
networks.example:
networks:
  prod:
    database:
      - as: db01
        last_octet: 11
    webserver:
      - as: web01
        last_octet: 12
  vdi:
    kali:
      - as: kali01
        last_octet: 201
      - as: kali02
        last_octet: 202
  vpn:
    wireguard:
      - as: wireguard
        last_octet: 5

extends.description: Name of another environment this one extends. The base is deep-merged in: scalar fields (teams, start, stop, root_password) the child sets win, otherwise they're inherited; vars/tags merge key-by-key (child wins); access windows and findings are the base's followed by the child's; the networks topology is a union, where the child's placement of an object on a network replaces the base's for that object. `teams` becomes optional here since it's inherited.
